Overview

What is guacamayo and how does it work?

Persistence — per session

Three identity skills share this board: /meta-wake reads it, /meta-grow refreshes it, /meta-dream finalizes it. /meta-dream is the sole transformer of identity files.

wake
session start

Loads the three seeds, reads this board and plan state, ingests cross-session context.

grow
mid-session

Captures growth entries, surfaces signals, refreshes the injected regions, overwrites the handover.

dream
session close

Writes the reflection, synthesizes seeds at 5+ entries, finalizes this board.

Workflow pipeline — per github issue

Groom to ship. A stage is done when its artifact exists: an issue, a plan doc, a green suite, a merged PR.

triage
  1. groombacklog issue
  2. /workflow-researchresearch doc
  3. /workflow-planplan doc · PLANNED
  4. /workflow-refineDoR gate → READY
→
build
  1. branch{PREFIX}-{NUM}-slug
  2. /workflow-executetests pass, lint clean
→
review
  1. /workflow-review12 dimensions · DoD
  2. commitRamsey commits, never Claude
  3. shipmake ship → merge → close
The Guacamayo Loop

Five nodes, one cycle. Every session generates telemetry; hooks enforce guardrails and record events; the metacognition skills derive patterns and propose changes; the retro graduates hypotheses into permanent config; improved config shapes the next session.

System Design

Three planes, one cycle. Plane 1 is where work happens — triage shapes an issue until it passes Definition of Ready, execute implements it, review measures it against Definition of Done. Plane 2 observes: the state board and identity lifecycle both write records, telemetry appends them, insights derive patterns, and a verification gate stands between a dashboard number and a retro hypothesis. Plane 3 is what retro actually changes — the four levers of the Claude setup, which shape every session on the planes above. Every box is a skill or module that actually fires; colour tracks which plane a record came from.

Plane 1 — triage → execute → review; triage and review each emit a record
Plane 2 — identity + board feed telemetry → insights → gate → retro
Plane 3 — the four levers a retro can pull

The state board sits in metacognition because it is a record, not a stage of work — triage writes to it via board.py, and /meta-wake and /meta-retro open and close issues directly. Dashed elements are stages that exist but are not automated — see Loop Health.

Cost & Efficiency

Where did the tokens go, and what did that effort buy?

North star Keep median cost per session declining while cache hit rate stays above 95%. Output tokens are the primary cost lever — fewer, denser responses beat long ones.

Effort is reported in cost units (input-price-relative), never USD — the weights are model-blind, so a dollar figure would be a lie. Cost is attributed to where effort was spent (repo, skill, subagent), not to work produced: Ramsey commits, so there is no commit→session join and any cost-per-commit ratio would read as Claude-authored output.

Session Health

How did my sessions actually run — and what pushed back?

North star Sessions run lean and land in one pass: peak context under the 150k cliff, few repeated turns, parallelism used where it helps. Friction — interruptions, tool failures, bash antipatterns — trends down; a pattern that recurs 3× gets a hook, not a note.
The 150k cliff: Sessions that grow past 150k context tokens cost 5× more per turn because the overflow can't be cached. In early July, 66-75% of sessions were hitting this cliff. The goal is <30%. Compaction is the mechanism — it compresses prior conversation to reclaim context space. Autocompact was broken Jul 15-18 (zero auto-triggered compactions despite sessions reaching 300k–557k tokens) and fired reliably every day since Jul 19 in the transcripts examined — but Ramsey reports it not firing in terminal mode (Jul 30 and again Jul 31). The Jul 30 investigation that found "no defect" read a VS Code session, so it never covered that surface. Treat this claim as contested pending a terminal-mode transcript.

Context Health

Is context under control? Are sessions staying lean?

North star Spend goes to the work, not to the scaffolding around it: skills and subagents earn their cost, context is compacted at phase boundaries rather than auto-rescued, and the failures that remain are guards firing — not malformed calls. A tool the harness keeps catching gets fixed at the source, not retried.

Loop Health

Is the three-plane architecture doing what the Overview says it does — and is the harness that watches it alive?

North star
Each plane runs end to end: work is triaged, executed and reviewed; metacognition turns telemetry into hypotheses; the control engine actually enforces. A plane that produces without consuming is not a loop — it is a pipe.
The three planes — where each one breaks

Same architecture as the Overview diagram, held to one schema so the missing stages are comparable. A dashed link means the next stage never receives what the previous one produced. Nodes carry a glyph as well as a colour.

Plane 1Work triage → execute → review closes, unevenly
✓
✓
✓
~
✓
triageexecutereviewpromoteDoD
3,483 findings · 272 blockers · 582 issues · 2 open inconsistencies · 114 plans unmatchable to an issue
~
Break: promotion is manual, and 111 plan docs carry no issue reference — drift is only detectable on the 37% that join.
Plane 2Metacognition telemetry → insights → gate → retro does not close
✓
✓
~
✓
✗
telemetryinsightsgateretroverify
1,641 sessions · 40 reflections · 14 retro rounds · 41 live hypotheses · 18 decisive in the latest run
✗
Break: the loop generates hypotheses faster than it can settle them, and nothing audits the backlog. See Experiments.
Plane 3Control engine the four levers a retro can pull pulls, rarely measures
✓
~
✗
✓
instructionscapabilitiesenforcementpersistence
2 unique hooks in the pass log (threshold 5) · 236 pass events recorded
✗
Break: the levers get pulled without a way to see whether they caught anything. Same shape as the R2 log_event graduation — the logger exists, the hooks do not call it.
◒
Read the breaks together. Plane 1 produces findings well. Plane 2 turns them into hypotheses well. Neither verifies, and Plane 3 cannot see whether its own controls fire. The system is strong at generating signal and weak at closing on it — which is one problem, appearing three times.

Hand-maintained: stage verdicts are architectural judgements, not derived metrics. Counts read 2026-08-19.

The harness — is the watcher watching?

Collection jobs

Every metric on this board is only as good as the job that collects it. These run under launchd (not cron — cron silently skips windows while the Mac sleeps). All of them report exit 0, so a stalled job looks identical to a healthy one unless recency is checked explicitly.

board
every 10 min
✓ healthy
Last successful run 10-29 11:19. Longest gap 9d (08-23 → 09-01).
facts
daily 09:00
✗ never ran
No successful run in the log window.
verdict scoring
per insights run
✓ healthy
Scored 41 hypotheses in the newest run (2026-10-29T10:28) across 74 recorded runs.
hook pass-log
per tool call
~ 2 of 5 hooks
2 unique hooks across 236 pass events (risky_git_guard 233, branch_guard 3). Breadth below 5 means hooks exit 0 without logging — unobservable, not absent.

Derived from logs/telemetry-*.log (exit-0 completions only), experiment_verdicts, and the hook pass log at render time. Cell state asserts on recency and breadth, never exit code.

⚑
The harness pattern. Three of four cells fail the same way: success and silence are the same signal. A job that never starts, a hook that exits 0 without logging, and a verdict with no registered metric all render as “fine”. The fix is uniform — assert on recency and breadth, not on exit code.
Pipeline health

Each stage of the metacognition pipeline — last run time and freshness. Green <24 h, yellow 1–7 d, red >7 d or never. Feedback is a permanent human gate — manual, but still aged, so a gate that never fires cannot hide behind a healthy loop.

Recurring friction

A rising badge means the most recent complete week exceeded 1.5× the mean of the three weeks before it; falling means it dropped below that mean by the same factor, from a base of at least three. Partial trailing weeks are excluded and unbadged rows are flat. Rising groups sort first — a pattern getting worse is more actionable than one that has been bad for a long time. Weeks are keyed on each finding's occurrence date (when the code was last touched), not on the day its review ran.

Experiments

Do retro recommendations become changes that actually get settled?

North star
Every retro recommendation becomes a hypothesis with a metric the system can observe, gets a verdict by its due date, and either graduates to permanent config or is reverted. An experiment nothing can measure is not an experiment — it is a note.
The measurement gap

Latest scoring run (2026-10-29): 41 hypotheses scored, 18 decisive. The rest carry a typed reason — a claim awaiting a collection change, a claim no telemetry could ever see, and a claim with no countable metric are different problems with different fixes.

CLA-78/LEB-78: `scripts/lint-parity.sh` + `scripts/tests/test-lint-parity.sh` — pre-commit ruff pin vs the version the repo actually resolves. Built because guacamayo#53 was closed asserting "pre-commit rev matches pyproject ruff version in all repos (verified)" while four repos disagreed; the word "verified" had no falsifier behind it. Fixed the one true break (`lebanese-blonde` pinned v0.11.2 against a resolved 0.16.0 — the literal false-green #53 described). **Method finding, the durable part**: the checker's first run reported 8 breaks, six of them phantom. `uv run ruff --version` in a repo that declares no ruff falls back to an *ambient* install (0.15.22 — the same value `/tmp` returns), so the pin was being compared against a binary CI never runs. One phantom (`ai-project-template` "reverse skew") had already been reported to Ramsey as a real finding before the surprising count triggered scrutiny. Discriminator added: only compare when the repo declares ruff in `pyproject.toml`; a dedicated regression fixture guards the false positive. Both directions demonstrated — planted defects took the suite to 9/2 and 10/1 from 11/0. **Outstanding, deliberately unfixed**: `job-system` declares ruff and resolves 0.16.0 but has no `ruff-pre-commit` hook at all (GAP — strictly worse than a skew), so the script still exits 1 by design; no allowlist added, since an allowlist is how a guard quietly stops guardingabsence:precommit-CI-lint-skew for 2 retro windows` + `presence:lint-parity-cited-in-all-repos-claimsinconclusive2026-08-022026-08-17
